utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everybody. Please be seated. Time doesn't cure everything, but I hope that the break served as a period for coming back to the spirit of cooperation we had earlier in this courtroom, and I hope that we can proceed in this spirit. But let us first hear the case number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Case number IT-97-24-T, the Prosecutor versus Milomir Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And the appearances, please, for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Nicholas Koumjian, Ann Sutherland, and Ruth Karper for the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Dan Cirkovic, our case manager, and John Ostojic on behalf of Mr. Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good afternoon, thank you. As usual, we have to start with some administrative matters. You may recall that on purpose we did not decide on the admission of the documents J8-1 until J8-23 before we had the Appeals Chamber decision. Having now this decision, it is necessary to admit these documents into evidence. I can't see any objections. Hereby admitted into evidence. We're extremely grateful that the registry provided us with the final Defence witness list. And we will proceed with the numbers you can find here, opposed to the 65 ter numbers we could find on the motions provided by the Defence. We have got the necessary proffers, save the following: Number 6, number 10, number 15, number 28, number 35, number 45, number 50, number 53, and number 56. This is only to recall that we need these statements proffered in due time. Let me also recall that the Chamber ordered that the appearances and the order of the appearances for the first eight working days in January 2003 should be available no later than 11 December. This would be Wednesday this week. We were confronted with some motions. May I ask, is it correct that the Defence does not want to come back to Witness Q? She would be available during these days.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: At this time, Your Honour, the Defence is of the position that we will not need Witness Q to ask her any further questions upon review of her transcript as well as the tapes and the transcript that we received in connection with her testimony under Rule 68 that the Prosecutor provided us. So we do not have any plans on asking for further cross-examination of Witness Q.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Shall I understand the first three words, "at this time," as a kind of caveat, or is it your find answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It's not a caveat, Your Honour. However, our investigator and Mr. Lukic is endeavouring to meet with the members that were identified late, and he has not completed that review. If during the interview process the individual whose testimony we would or hopefully utilise to attack or at least add some credibility or weight to Witness Q, then we would formally file a motion, we anticipate, for leave to do so. We'd hate to speculate on that point, but at this point, reviewing her transcript and reviewing the testimony provided by the 68 individual, we do not believe there's a need. However, during the interview if something arises, we will let the Court know. But at this point it is a final answer, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes. But please be aware then this does not fall under the attempt to cure that you might call as a prejudice happening on the basis that some statements were not provided in due time to the Defence. This would be a matter emanating in an ordinary cause of hearing the one or other witness in preparation of their hearing, and then it would be an ordinary case but not under the extraordinary circumstances emanating from the fact that some statements were not provided in due time. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: With all due respect to the Court, I don't necessarily agree in entirety with the Court's summary, and I'll explain why, if I may. In essence, we believe that the Defence was prejudiced, as we outlined. We believe that even if we were to re-examine Witness Q, the benefit of that re-examination has been lost forever because now she would have been otherwise more fully prepared in light of knowing exactly what questions we would ask her. This is -- then it would be her second attempt or second opportunity to testify, so she would now be a more experienced witness. When the Court under the Rules is given the authority to judge the credibility of a witness, it is also obviously to make observations of the witness while they're testifying. We, the Defence, feel that we've lost that opportunity with respect to a number of witnesses. I recognise the Court does not agree with us. It is not a cure, in my opinion, although we're grateful that the OTP recognises the late disclosure, it is not a cure, we believe, in hindsight to go back and ask limited questions. We'll do so in the interest of justice, but by no means will we take the position that it is an absolute cure and therefore no prejudice resulted. We will maintain our position and we will be steadfast in that position, the Defence had lost an opportunity and we were not given what we consider and deem to be a fair trial. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think to make the record clear for purpose obviously the Defence is setting up an appeal issue. It should be clear in the record that the Office of the Prosecutor sent a letter to the Defence, I believe, dated the -- about a week ago, indicating that Witness Q would be brought here and the Defence would be allowed to question Witness Q if they had any further questions. The statement that counsel is speaking about is, as Your Honours know, the statement of the person that she named as the perpetrator of crimes against her, very, very serious crimes against her. The name of that person was available to the Defence before the trial when her statement was provided. So if the Defence has not yet spoken to that person, it's not due to any fault of the Office of the Prosecutor. The fact that that individual denies his very serious crime, I don't think anyone can realistically say that they're surprised that in an interview with the Office of the Prosecutor that this person did not admit his crimes. But in any event, we are prepared at this time to have Witness Q available if the Defence has any further questions, and we believe that in fairness to her, if they have any further questions, they should ask them to her when she is in The Hague on this occasion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: To make the transcript absolutely clear, you referred to a letter from 3 December 2002 sent via facsimile and locker to Defence counsel Lukic. And in response to this, we received a letter or a facsimile by Defence counsel Ostojic from December 4, 2002, indicating that the intention would be to put to Witness Q some additional questions. And I understand from the submission we heard today by the Defence counsel that this request is now withdrawn, because it's out of question that whenever there should be a question to Witness Q, it should be when she is here and not to cause additional harm to Witness Q. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We do, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then may I formally ask whether protective measures are requested for the witness of today -- or the first witness of today, number 005.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. First of all, I'd like to on the record thank the Court for granting our motion to amend the witness list, and also I'm grateful to the Office of the Prosecutor and Mr. Koumjian for accepting this change. It was unanticipated. We cite the reasons in the motion. We are grateful and thankful for the opportunity to present these witnesses in the order that we suggest in light of the personal handicap that is the prior witnesses have apparently experienced in the last two weeks. With respect to the Court's question on a pseudonym. The first witness, Witness number 005, we are seeking full protective measures, including name, pseudonym, voice, and face distortion. And I can, if the Court wishes, in private session explain why.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Any objections by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then the pseudonym, this would be DD, is granted and voice and face distortion is granted. Do we need any additional time or break preparation for this? Thank you. May we -- before asking Witness 005, now DD, entering the courtroom, may we hear what is your perspective as regards the other witnesses of this week?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We'd also be making an application for the same protective measures as we have for Witness named DD for the second witness that will be called, which is Witness number 044.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And the estimated time you would need for the envisaged all in all six witnesses?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We think that we can finish well before Friday, Your Honour, for all six.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Let's try to do our very best. It was not possible to tell the parties during the last hearing that the same day in the afternoon we got the message that the Judge's plenary was rescheduled starting Thursday this week. So we should try to do our very best. Take all the time you need, but nevertheless we should try to do the best in order to enable the Judges to participate in part -- at least in part in the plenary. But this shouldn't be the obstacle. Our first purpose and work is no doubt to hear the evidence prepared by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understood the Court. If the plenary occurs on Friday, is it for one day or is it for the two days?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It starts Friday in the morning and continues on -- it starts on Thursday in the morning and continues until Friday.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Because one of our witnesses, a further application that we would ask with respect to Witness number 068, he has not arrived with other individuals that have, the other witnesses. He is scheduled to arrive Thursday evening -- Wednesday evening. We were going to make an application today to ask that we either reschedule the hearing and proceed Thursday afternoon so that I could meet with the witness. I have not done so yet. He is not here, as I've stated. Or in the alternative, we were going to seek if we could hear this final witness on Friday, as the final witness. We anticipate that we should be able to conclude the five witnesses that are present at The Hague by the end of the session Wednesday afternoon or evening at 7.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Let's go into the details of Witness 068 by Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Any other administrative matters? Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Oh, sorry. Thank you. We also were going to make an application, perhaps it's the appropriate time now, for the next witness, 044, pseudonym, face distortion. So I'm not sure if the record reflects that that's -- if the OTP has an objection to it and what the Court's ruling is on that. He's similarly situated as Witness 005. And again we can describe in detail why we believe there's a necessity for it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Are there objections by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Granted. And this will be then DE. The Prosecution wanted to take the floor. Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I'm just going to inquire if it's at all possible to have that witness come a day earlier so that we can hear the witness Thursday morning, rather than have an empty Thursday. If it's at all possible to reschedule that witness to come. Because I realise that counsel would probably have to work on that now with the Victims and Witnesses Unit, reschedule the last witness to come a day earlier so he's available Thursday morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We're grateful for any suggestion that the OTP has. I stand corrected with the number. It was witness number 071 first of all that is not here, who is arriving Wednesday evening. There are many options available to us. One is that we can tell this witness not to show up, 071, until the first session in January. If -- if the Court permits or if all can agree on it. 068 is present. He will proceed as scheduled. 071 was the witness that I mentioned earlier who is arriving Wednesday evening, and we feel we need an opportunity to meet with him, as the OTP has had an opportunity to meet with all their witnesses prior to their testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Is it correct that this would take us no longer than one day session?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then let's discuss this issue of 071 on Wednesday. Anything else? May I then ask that Witness DD be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. Can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May we please hear your solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course. Shall I begin? I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated, and please understand that you will be addressed in this courtroom not with your name but you will be called Witness or Witness DD. This is a protective measure in your own interest on request of the Defence. Please, the Defence may start.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness DD.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: My name is John Ostojic, and along with our case manager, Danilo Cirkovic, we represent Dr. Milomir Stakic. I'm going to ask you a series of questions here today. First of all, I'd like with the Court's permission to advise you that the Court has granted our request that you be given a pseudonym, which is now DD, and that there be facial and voice distortion. You understand that, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: With the Court's permission, if the usher would be kind enough to show the witness this piece of paper; first, of course, to the OTP. Witness DD, the usher was kind enough to show you a piece of paper which is in front of you. Can you tell us what's written on that paper.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: My first and last name.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: For the record, if we could admit that document, Your Honour, as the next Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This will be admitted into evidence as D41.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If we may mark it confidential within the exhibit list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This goes without saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. May I proceed, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Witness DD, can you please give us your date of birth.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Yes, I can. I was born on the 7th of January, 1970.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us of your marital status.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: My marital status is that I'm married and I have one child.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Where do you presently reside? In what town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Currently in Ljubija.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you share with us, if you know, how many kilometres that is away from the town of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Ljubija is 12 kilometres away from the town of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: In what municipality is Ljubija in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: It belongs to Prijedor municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And in the spring and summer of 1992, in what municipality was the town of Ljubija within?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: It belongs to Prijedor municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you share with us, please, your ethnic background.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: I am Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether both your parents are Serbian.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: My father is a Serb, and my mother is a Croat. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And forgive me for asking, sir, what is the ethnic background of your wife?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: My wife is also a Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Tell me, if you will: In the spring and summer of 1992, where did you reside?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: At that time I was in Ljubija.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Quickly, if I may, can you share with us your educational background. What is the highest level of education that you attained and where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: I completed my secondary education in 1988 in Prijedor, the fourth grade of secondary education.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What was your area of study or concentration, if any?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: It was a school for agriculture and nutritionism, and my occupation is I'm an agricultural technician.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Briefly, share with us if you served in the military at any time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Yes. That was before the war. I did my regular military service.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you share with us for what period to what period did you serve in the military.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: I served from the 16th of May, 1989, to the 15th of May, 1990.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you have any area of specialty within the military that you concentrated on during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: I was a tank driver, a driver of the M-84 tank. That was my specialty in the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm now going to turn, Witness DD, to an issue regarding your employment history. I'd like with the Court's permission to go into closed session with respect to that. The Defence believes if revealed where he presently is employed, it may jeopardise the pseudonym and the protective measures granted by the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It's good you asked this question right now, because I just wanted to do the same for procedural matters. Let us please go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: A couple more points if I may, Witness DD, to testify. During your capacity in which you were employed from June of 1992 through February 1993, did you have an opportunity to observe people who were working and were gainfully employed in the Prijedor hospital in the very city of Prijedor? From June 1992 through, at the very least, September 30th of 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Yes. All employees of the Prijedor hospital were receiving their salaries.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me just, in order to be a little more precise and concrete: Did you during this period of June 1992 through September 30th, 1992, observe that members of all three ethnic groups within the Prijedor municipality continued to work in both the health centre in Ljubija and the Prijedor hospital in the city of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: As concerns Ljubija, I'm sure about that. Yes, they were there, because I worked there too. As far as the main hospital in Prijedor is concerned, I couldn't be entirely sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: In your function from June of 1992 through February 1993, did you have an opportunity to take citizens of the Prijedor municipality to the Prijedor hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Yes, I did on a daily basis, whenever I had a task to accomplish.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you just describe for us the type of people, meaning the injuries that they may have sustained, that you would take them from the health centre in Ljubija to the Prijedor hospital. What type of injuries are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Personally, I couldn't tell you much about their injuries, but I was following the orders given to me by the doctor who was on duty, and I was driving all the people who needed medical assistance, regardless of their national, ethnic, or political background.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: For example, Witness DD, would you take a woman who was pregnant and ready to give birth to her child? Would you be the one who would drive her from the health centre in Ljubija to the Prijedor hospital upon the orders of the physician?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Yes. And that's what I was doing. That was my duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you, sir, also drive during this time period of June 1992 through September 30th, 1992, and beyond citizens who were of the Muslim ethnicity from Ljubija to the Prijedor hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Yes, both Muslims and Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: As well as Serbs, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: That's understood.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And was there at any time any request by anyone to prohibit you from driving any citizens in need of medical care and treatment from the area of the Ljubija health centre to the Prijedor hospital which would have in any way or manner prevented you from taking those citizens to the hospital in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: No. That's a fairly short and simple answer. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So is it fair, sir, that during the entire time that you were employed in the capacity in which you described, that you continued to drive people who were in need of medical care and treatment to the Prijedor hospital regardless of their ethnic background or composition, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: That's correct, as I've said before.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The period immediately prior to April 1992, where were you residing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: I was residing with my parents in our family house.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That is located in what town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: That's also in Ljubija.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: With the Court's permission, if we can show the witness Exhibit S1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If the usher would be kind enough to assist us. If I may also ask Your Honour if the exhibit would be placed on the ELMO so that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We'd appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Witness DD, there's a map that's been introduced and admitted into evidence of the municipality of Prijedor that we have placed on the ELMO. I'm going to ask you if you can be kind enough to point out where did you reside during the spring and summer of 1992? Where were you living?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: This is the place, Ljubija. That's where I grew up and I have lived this whole time.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I recognise you may not know this, but it is shaded in green and there's a chart on the top left-hand corner indicating what it means when a town is marked in green. Can you share with us how far, in terms of kilometres, Hambarine is to the town of Ljubija. We see it on the map, but if you could just tell us how many kilometres away it is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: About 8 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us briefly how far away your home in the spring and summer of 1992 was from the Ljubija soccer stadium or football stadium, as they call it in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: My house is about 700 metres away from the pitch, the stadium.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Tell us now, during the time that you were describing your employment of driving from the Ljubija health centre in the Prijedor hospital, basically what route, if you could just share with us using this map, what route would you take?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Ljubija-Hambarine-Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How often in the spring and summer of 1992 did you make the trip from Ljubija to the town of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Until the moment the war broke out, I went on an everyday basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: With respect to the period that we're discussing, prior to April of 1992, can you describe for us the atmosphere in terms of the general situation for the population in the Prijedor municipality.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: People stayed at their homes, regardless of their ethnic background.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you describe for us what the situation was in terms of the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. economy. Was it a problem? Was it running smoothly at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Well, problems were beginning to show because there was a war raging in neighbouring Croatia, and due to that very fact, the economy was faltering. Salaries decreased and they were not paid regularly.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Was there an anxiety and tension within your community and that which you observed within the city of Prijedor in the municipality of Prijedor in the spring and summer of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: There was an amount of anxiety at that time because all ethnicities were afraid of war, and their existence itself was in danger.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: A couple more questions with respect to Exhibit S1. Can you tell me within that town of Ljubija that you lived, to the best of your knowledge, information, and observations, were any homes burned in the spring and summer of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: In Ljubija itself, during that period not a single house was burnt down.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: In the period, just so that I'm clear and so you understand that I'm using this period, because it's a period that's reflected within the indictment that's filed against Dr. Stakic -- the period that not one house was burned in your town of Ljubija, is that true for the period of April 30th, 1992, through September 30th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: That is certainly true of the Ljubija area.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, were you at any time discriminated against - and again, the time period I'd like to confine it to, April through September 1992 - in light of the fact that your mother is Croatian?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: There weren't any problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did anyone intimidate or harass you during that time period, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: No one did, not in any sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: At that time, sir, certainly you had an opportunity to listen to the radio, to watch television, and to read the newspapers. Did you at any time, sir, hear or learn of any propaganda to promote any type of aggression against non-Serbs, namely Muslims and Croats, in the Prijedor municipality in the spring and summer of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: No, I never heard anything like that. And as far as I was told later, there had been no such propaganda to begin with, especially as concerns the civilian structures of the government.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just so that we understand your area and the town that you lived in, there was Donja Ljubija and Gornja Ljubija, correct, and Ljubija itself, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Ljubija is a whole, and then there are two constituent parts, Gornja and Donja Ljubija as a local commune.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. In Donja Ljubija, can you tell me what the ethnic composition was of the homes that were in that area.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: In terms of percentage, 95 per cent were Bosniaks. The remaining 5 per cent were Serbs and Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What about Gornja Ljubija?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: In Gornja Ljubija, the situation was more mixed in terms of percentage also. Roughly speaking, 25 per cent of the population were Muslims and 30 or 35 per cent each Croats and Serbs respectively.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: A couple more questions, if you don't mind, on background. Prior to April of 1992, were you a member or affiliated with a political party?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: No, not prior to April 1992. I was not a member of any political party.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Were you a member of a political party of April 1992? And if so, tell us when and which party.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: After April 1992, I became a member of the SDS; at some point in July 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: For how long, sir, did you maintain membership within that political party?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: For about a year.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you, sir, prior to April 1992 become familiar with the name of Dr. Milomir Stakic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Yes. I heard the name in the media.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What did you hear of Dr. Milomir Stakic prior to April 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Prior to April 1992, I heard Dr. Stakic's name and I heard that he was the vice-president of the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Prior to April 1992, did you ever hear Dr. Milomir Stakic give a speech or an interview which would be deemed discriminatory against any ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: No, I didn't. And later on I learnt that Mr. Stakic was not engaged in any propaganda in any type of the media.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And let me clarify, just so that my questions come out proper. So prior to April 1992, you're not aware or didn't hear of any propaganda that would be attributed to Dr. Stakic which can be deemed in some manner as being discriminatory. Subsequent, or after April of 1992, through the period of the spring and summer of 1992, did you personally, sir, hear or were you ever told that Dr. Stakic at any time issued any speeches or statements which would in any manner even remotely be considered to be discriminatory against any ethnic group within the Prijedor municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Personally, I didn't hear anything. And in subsequent conversations with the -- with people in my village, I did not hear anything that would tie Dr. Stakic with any form of propaganda that would be discriminatory against the Serbian population or would call for the ethnic cleansing of the non-Serb population or any other form of discrimination.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me just be permitted to clarify that answer, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you hear -- and you likewise didn't hear any discriminatory speeches made by Dr. Stakic against non-Serbs, correct? In other words, to the best of my recollection, to the best of your observations during that time, having lived in the Prijedor municipality, you did not observe or hear that Dr. Stakic gave or issued any discriminatory remarks against, for example, the Bosniak Muslims or the Croats or any other non-Serbs, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: That is absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Witness DD, are you a friend of Dr. Stakic's?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: I don't know Dr. Stakic personally. I have never been introduced to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So in the spring and summer of 1992, you did not know Dr. Stakic, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: That is correct. I didn't know him personally, but I heard of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: I knew what position he was in.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And you never met him during the spring and summer of 1992, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: That is correct, but I never personally met him.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And subsequent or after the spring and summer of 1992, did you have an opportunity to personally meet or become acquainted with Dr. Stakic in any manner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: No, I didn't have such an opportunity.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: One other general question, if I may, with respect to mobilisation: Were you aware, sir, that in 1991 there was a call-up for mobilisation, a compulsory mobilisation was issued by the military? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Yes, I know that personally. That is correct. The Yugoslav People's Army, which existed at the time, issued call-up papers for compulsory mobilisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Help me with this, since you were in the military for some time, and in your current capacity you may be also familiar with that. The call-up for mobilisation is issued by the military, correct? In other words, it is not issued by the civilian police departments or units, and it's certainly not issued by the local politicians within a municipality, correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I object to counsel testifying and giving answers to the witness. We should ask the witness the questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sustained.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me, Witness DD, who is it that issues the call-up for mobilisation generally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Generally it is the army who does that. And at the time, it was the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It was the army when you served during your military service that would issue these mobilisations, correct? That is, in 1988, as you've identified.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: That's correct. It was the army who would issue such call-up papers. And prior to the beginning of the war, it was also the task of the military, the army, to issue such call-up papers.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So in 1991, it was the army who issued it. And even to this day, sir, it's the army who issues the compulsory mobilisation of men of military age, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may direct your attention to the period of April 30th, 1992, Witness DD. We've for all practical purposes, if I can say, have kind of identified this as a date, so I'm using it for purposes of your testimony as well. Do you recall on or about April 30th, 1992, what occurred in the Prijedor municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: I remember that date. That was the 30th of April, and then the 1st of May of 1992 there was a takeover of government in Prijedor municipality. The Serbs took over.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you describe for us, if you will, whether it was a violent or non-violent takeover.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: It was non-violent, and it was the army that took over. But I would like to point out that on that particular day during the takeover of power, nobody was injured or killed or harassed in any way, or put in simple terms, no bullet was fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'd like to take you through the period of April 30th, 1992, through May 22nd, 1992. As the Court has heard, as the OTP has introduced and led evidence, I believe that on or about May 22nd, 1992, was a significant date in the Prijedor municipality because it related to an incident that occurred. Do you remember that on May 22nd, 1992, that an incident occurred in the Prijedor municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: I remember the date and the incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just if you can tell me, where did the incident on May 22nd, 1992, take place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: That incident took place in Pod Hambarine or the so-called field of Prijedor, Prijedorsko Polje, during the afternoon hours of 22nd of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: On the map is to your right on the ELMO, can you indicate the place, although I think we can see it, on Exhibit S1, where this incident on May 22nd, 1992, occurred.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: It was somewhere around here.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just so the record is clear, the witness indicated above and to the right -- slightly above and to the right of the green dot which bears underneath the town name of Hambarine, for clarification purposes. I'll get back to this incident in a few moments. I'd like us to focus if we can now on the period between April 30th, 1992, the takeover, as you've identified it, and the incident at Hambarine on May 22nd, 1992. Did you, sir, during that time period of approximately three weeks, three-plus weeks, did you have an opportunity to travel from your home in Ljubija to the city town of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Yes. I had an opportunity to travel every day; not just me, but all the other citizens of Ljubija, regardless of their ethnic background.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So for that period of time, April 30th through May 22nd, 1992, citizens of the Prijedor municipality freely and actively travelled from, at the very least, your home town of Ljubija to the city town of Prijedor, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: That is correct. They travelled either by their own personal vehicles or by public transportation.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I recognise you were a relatively young man at that time. Can you share with us, if you will, the purpose of your travels from Ljubija to the city centre town of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: I travelled for various purposes. Prijedor was the centre of that municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you travel to socialise with other friends, neighbours from within the municipality? Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: That is correct, and also to obtain some things for everyday life. All the municipal structures of authority are in Prijedor: The police, and the places where we could obtain documents. So everything is in Prijedor; that's why we went there.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: During that period of April 30th through May 22nd, 1992, did you observe that these institutions that you identified were working and continued to work in the same manner as they had prior to April 30th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: It was obvious. Everything continued as before.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Was there at any time during this period, sir, an outbreak of violence or social disorder that you observed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: No, there was no violence against anybody. Although, there was a surge of tensions.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And why is that, sir? If you know.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: People were afraid of war. They were afraid because the economic situation deteriorated. They were afraid of having to go on the dole, to become unemployed. So they were scared for their livelihood.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Was there an exodus or a forcible transfer of Muslims or Croatians during -- let me repeat the question. I apologise. I had the mic off. Sir, to the best of your observations and recollection, during the period of April 30th, 1992, through May 22nd, 1992, did you observe any forced transfers of non-Serbs from the Prijedor municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: I didn't observe anything like that, and it didn't take place at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And share with us why you say that it did not take place.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Nobody felt the need to move anywhere, because nobody was harassed during that period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And likewise, during that period of time, no one was involuntarily forcing citizens of Prijedor to leave their respective homes, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: That is correct. Not even the military structures did that, let alone the civilian authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, turning to the date of the incident at Hambarine, May 22nd, 1992. You were in the Prijedor municipality, specifically in your town, I believe, of Ljubija. Can you describe for us what is it that you learned that occurred with respect to the incident that we've identified at Hambarine which occurred on May 22nd, 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: I learnt about the incident on the evening of the same day, and I learned that some people, that is, some soldiers, had been killed in that place.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you learn, sir, from what area the soldiers were coming from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Yes, I did. The soldiers were members of the Yugoslav People's Army, which existed at the time, and they were on their way back from Manjaca training ground, and it was the weekend, so they were on the way back home, to their homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Using the map that's to your right, Exhibit S1, identify for us, if you know or can find the area of Manjaca. If you could.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Well, it's not going to be. This is a map of --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm just not sure if the witness could generally. But with the Court's permission, we'd like to show him a different map. And perhaps he could help us with that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Yes, thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: S14, for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If the usher would be kind enough to place Exhibit S14 on the ELMO. And, Witness DD, utilising this exhibit, can you show us, please, where these JNA soldiers, some of whom were killed at Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Hambarine on May 22nd, 1992, were coming from.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Here I can't see Manjaca training ground. It is not on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Perhaps at the break we'll be able to clarify that and we could come back to this question, with the Court's permission, I think. Thank you. Describe for me to the extent that you know how many soldiers were in this vehicle that were attacked on or about May 22nd, 1992, at Hambarine.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: It was a Golf vehicle. There were six members of the Yugoslav People's Army in that vehicle. Four of them were Serbs, and two of them were Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And subsequent to that date of that incident, you became aware of who those individuals specifically were, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you list for us, to the best of your recollection, their names.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: I may not be able to recall all of their names, at least not their first names. But I know all of their family names. There was a guy called Lukic. He was shot dead. There was another one called Milojica who was also shot dead. Ratko Milojica who was the first Milojica's cousin, he was injured. Sinisa Mijatovic was injured, Nedeljko Antunovic, and Miroslav Lujic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please, your microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you come to learn, Witness DD, who was it that shot at these JNA soldiers and ultimately killing two and wounding two?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: I learnt later on that those were Muslims, that is, inhabitants of Hambarine.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you at that time, sir, subsequent to the incident that occurred on May 22nd, 1992 -- or I should say, immediately thereafter, did you hear over the radio or television an ultimatum that was issued to the residents of Hambarine?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Yes. It -- I did hear that on Radio Prijedor. This was issued by the military authorities in order to have the perpetrators of that crime extradited. The ultimatum was issued for the perpetrators to be extradited by the following day, by noon of the following day. So they wanted the perpetrators to surrender by the following noon.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just so that we're clear in the couple moments that we have before our break, which I'm anticipating, did you at that time hear of any ultimatums given by any of the civilian authorities within the Prijedor municipality involving the incident of Prijedor and this ultimatum?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: I didn't hear of any. None of the locals informed me about any such thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And the ultimatum that you heard to the citizens or the residents of Hambarine came from the military, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That ultimatum, sir, was strictly confined - I believe your testimony was - that the perpetrators of the attack on the Serb -- on the soldiers of the JNA, which killed two Serbs and wounded two others, Croats as well, that they be turned over to the authorities; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: That is correct. They were to turn over to the military authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Was there a specific leader within that town that the military authorities perceived as the critical perpetrator of the crime against its soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: The military authorities at the time blamed the person called Aziz Aliskovic, who was, so to say, the leader of that group.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, sir, did the ultimatum ask that all the citizens turn themselves in as a result of this incident on May 22nd, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: No. They just wanted the perpetrators to turn themselves in, not the rest of the local population.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I understand. I just want to record to be ultimately clear. Did this ultimatum, sir, that the military issued on May 22nd, 1992, as a result of this incident on the JNA soldier, did they request that all the citizens of the town of Hambarine turn in their weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, this was not required at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did the ultimatum require, sir, that all the citizens of the town of Hambarine who were of military age turn themselves in to the army or the military authorities as a result of the incident wherein the JNA soldiers were attacked, killed, and wounded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: No. It didn't apply to all men of military age but only to the perpetrators, the direct perpetrators of that crime, the direct participants in that incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The trial stands adjourned until 4.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated. And please continue immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Witness DD, a couple more questions with respect to the incident that occurred at Hambarine on May 22nd, 1992. To the best of your recollection and observation, was the ultimatum that was issued by the military accepted by the perpetrators of this crime?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: The ultimatum was not accepted by noon on the 23rd of May, 1992, so the army extended the ultimatum by another 15 minutes, in the hope that the perpetrators would be surrendered, which did not take place.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The ultimatum issued by the army was not accepted with respect to this incident relating to Hambarine. Before I ask you what occurred after the ultimatum was issued and after it was not accepted, give us to the best of your recollection, having lived only several kilometres from Hambarine and passing through there from time to time, describe for us how many homes first are in this region that has been identified as the Brdo area.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And I'd ask with the Court's permission that the usher again tender to you to be shown on the ELMO Exhibit S1.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So first, if you may, describe for us what is it that this region, which is known as the Brdo region, what towns would it include?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: The area referred to as the Brdo area contains a number of villages, the following one: Hambarine, Carakovo, Rizvanovici, Rakovcani, Biscani.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: In this Brdo area, can you tell us how many homes approximately are there or were there in the spring and summer of 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number, but there must be between four and five thousand homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And now, to be a little more precise with respect to the town of Hambarine, approximately how many homes, to the best of your recollection, having lived there most, if not all of your life, were there within this town of Hambarine?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: In the town of Hambarine itself, perhaps several hundred, between six and seven hundred homes, I'd say. That's my best estimate.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: After the ultimatum was not accepted by the perpetrators who attacked the JNA soldiers on May 22nd, 1992, what, if anything, occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: After that, at around 20 minutes past noon on the 23rd of May, the shelling of houses began, houses located between the Prijedor Polje, and the highest point near Hambarine. The shelling -- the road, the Ljubija-Prijedor road was shelled and only the area where the road was was shelled.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you, sir, have an opportunity after the shelling or after May 22nd, 1992, to pass through this Ljubija-Prijedor road which had been shelled?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Two or three days later you could use the road, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you, sir, at any time subsequent to May 22nd, 1992, pass through the road and make personal observations of the homes that were shelled?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Yes, I did use the road. The first time was on the 6th of June, 1992. I was going somewhere on duty, and I saw the amount of destruction that had occurred up to that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us to the best of your recollection what your observations were at that point, namely, how many roads on that road, in that town, and in that village and in that region were shelled or destroyed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: About 40 or 50 houses had been shelled, houses, as I've said, located between the highest point inside Hambarine and a place referred to as the Prijedor Polje, halfway through the Prijedor Polje. Just off the road, to the left and to the right of the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may, with the Court's permission.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I thought, Mr. Witness DD, that you said maximally or at a maximum of 50 homes. I'm not asking you to change your -- alter your testimony. The record reflects that you said 40 to 50. But I thought you said approximately 40, maximally 50 homes. Could you just, to be more precise and accurate, share with us that what you observed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: As concerns the number, the number was between 40 and 50 homes. I saw destroyed houses with roofs destroyed. Some houses had burnt down due to the shelling. And those homes were abandoned, empty.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And the homes that you saw near the Polje, as you described, were the homes where the incident wherein those two JNA soldiers were fatally shot and the two others were wounded, correct? That was generally the area where this incident that we've identified of May 22nd, 1992, occurred, correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Objection. Counsel leading the witness, suggesting answers to the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sustained.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, Witness DD, approximately, with respect to the homes that were targeted and where the incident occurred on May 22nd, 1992, the relationship between those two.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Well, I don't know the real relationship, but I think it must have been the fury of the military because their requests for the perpetrators of the crime that had taken place to be surrender was not accepted.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The homes beyond the road, of the Ljubija-Prijedor road, that were not at its highest peaks, they were not shelled and were not burned, at least at the time that you observed them, namely, after June 6th, 1992, correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Objection. Counsel leading the witness, suggesting answers. He hasn't testified to that so far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] I believe the witness did indeed --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Dismissed. Please answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you answer the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm afraid I didn't understand the question. Can I please have the question repeated.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And I'll read it just so that we're clear: "The homes beyond the road of the Ljubija-Prijedor road that were not at its highest peaks, they were not shelled and were not burned, at least at the time that you observed them, namely, after June 6th, 1992, correct?"

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: That's correct. Those homes had not been burned. They were still inhabited.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just going back to one issue that we covered. I forgot to ask you this, with respect to the mobilisation: At the time of 1992, sir, you were approximately 22 years of age, the mobilisation in 1991, were you asked to serve - excuse me - in the military in 1991?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: At any time after the mobilisation calls in September and November of 1991, were you ever called to be mobilised with the army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: No. I was not mobilised, nor had I ever received any call-up papers, nor did I volunteer for military service, for that matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And do you know why it is that you were not called for mobilisation or for service in 1991 or thereafter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: I don't know. I never received the mobilisation call-up. It was never given to me. So no one looked for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, going back to the chronology. Following May 22nd, 1992, the incident at Hambarine, did you become, sir, familiar with another incident that occurred on or about May 24th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: I believe there was an incident in Kozarac, or more specifically, the hamlet of Jakupovici. That's also near the Prijedor-Banja Luka road.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If you could just point to the area where this incident at Kozarac on May 24th, 1992, occurred. And we're talking about the map to your right, which is S1.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: It was here.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So that the record is clear, the witness was pointing to an area to the left, if we're facing the map, of the green dot with the name above it "Kozarac," which is to the right to the village of Kozarusa.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What, sir, did you learn about the incident of May 24th, 1992, at Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: I learned that a military group with a freight motor vehicle was moving from Banja Luka -- was supposed to be moving from Banja Luka in the direction of Prijedor, and the then-military authorities requested that all physical obstacles be removed. That would make it impossible for the military personnel to pass through or the military vehicles towards Prijedor, referring to at least 100 metres to the left or to the right of the road itself. This request was not complied with, and then a freight motor vehicle came along at some point in the afternoon or the evening on the 24th of May. The vehicle reached this point, this critical point, and was fired at. The driver of the lorry - I can't remember his name - was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: These physical obstacles that you described, were they road barricades or checkpoints placed within the Banja Luka-Prijedor road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: I can't say exactly whether those were barricades or checkpoints, but there were groups of armed people there, Bosniaks, who controlled that section of the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And that area, sir, predominantly consisted of citizens of Prijedor municipality of what ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: They were predominantly Bosniaks. Bosniak population predominantly, about 99 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Was there, sir, a military response to this incident and attack on this freight motor vehicle convoy passing through the Banja Luka-Prijedor road on May 24th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: I think there was another ultimatum for the perpetrators of that incident, of that crime, to be turned over. And again, this ultimatum was not met with. And then the members of the army started to shell the Kozarac area.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Who issued the ultimatum after the military freight vehicle and convoy were attacked that we've identified as the incident on May 24th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: I don't personally know who it was, but I know that it was issued by the then-JNA, Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know if the civilian police within the Prijedor municipality issued any such ultimatums as a result of this incident on May 24th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: The civilian police, I'm sure, didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Likewise, do you know or did you hear at that time whether the civilian authorities in the Prijedor municipality issued any type of ultimatum relating to the incident, namely the attack on the JNA freight Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. motor vehicle passing through the Banja Luka-Prijedor road on or about May 24th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: At that time we, the locals, were familiar with the military and security situation through the media, but personally I heard nothing in the media that the civilian authorities in Prijedor might have been in charge of.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Following the refusal of the ultimatum issued by the military, as you've identified and testified to, the military responded and attacked the Kozarac area, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: The town of Kozarac and the surrounding hamlets were attacked.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The next incident, if you will, that we have identified is on or about May 30th, 1992. Are you familiar, sir, with what, if any, significance that date has?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: I know about that particular incident. We refer to it as the attack on Prijedor or the clash between the Yugoslav People's Army and the armed groups of Bosniaks, mostly Bosniaks, who did not belong to any of the JNA units.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'll just back up with a couple of questions. Would this, sir, be -- or tell us, because I don't want to lead -- tell us how many incidents occurred in roughly what period of time, starting with the incident in Hambarine, up to and including the incident at the attack on Prijedor on May 30th, 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Well, between these two dates, the only incident was the one at Kozarac on the 24th, as we have just stated. But there were no other incidents apart from that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So those three incidents within that approximate eight- to nine-day period, correct? From the 22nd through the 30th.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Yes. I'm talking about the one at Kozarac. There were no other incidents of any kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, describe for us, to the best of your recollection, having lived in the area and travelled through Prijedor in the spring and summer of 1992, who attacked the town of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: You mean the 30th of May?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I do.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: The attack was carried out by armed groups of Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How did you come to learn that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: I learned that through the media, Radio Prijedor, which was providing news on the situation on the ground all the time, news concerning the political and security situation throughout Prijedor municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know the size of this group that attacked the town of Prijedor on May 30th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: I can't remember the exact size. I think there must have been about 200 armed members of these groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just so that I'm clear and so that I don't misunderstand, this was neither a small group nor a resistance group that attacked the town of Prijedor on May 30th, 1992, correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Objection. Counsel is putting words into the witness's mouth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: That's a normal problem with leading and misleading questions. Sustained.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I just may be heard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On paragraph 18 of the 4th amended indictment, specifically the charge as laid out by the Prosecutor seems to indicate that they've captioned and coined this attack as a resistance group. This witness, as counsel has from time to time asked us, the Defence, to put our case to the witnesses. We simply are asking this witness, one, does he constitute this 200 Bosniak Muslims who attacked Prijedor quantifyingly as small, as the OTP does on paragraph 18? And how is it that he would classify them as attackers or a resistance group, as they do within their indictment? I think we have an obligation to clarify that issue, although we can make the argument in our briefs, as well as orally, I think it's necessary -- and we are trying to confine it specifically to the 4th amended indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Just briefly, Your Honour. Rule 90(H), which deals with putting your case to the witness, only applies of course to cross-examination. Counsel are not allowed to state what they want a witness to say to their own witness in order to get a favourable answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: As I said earlier, sustained.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Could you describe for us, sir, the nature and extent of the attack by the Bosniak Muslims on the town of Prijedor on May 30th, 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: They attacked the JNA. One of the soldiers was seriously wounded. He was the commander of a platoon or a squad, Zoran Karlica. Two days later, Zoran Karlica died from the wounds received on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Was there, if any, resistance to the attack by the Bosniak Muslims of the town of Prijedor on or about May 30th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: There was only resistance against those who were firing their weapons at members of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Was there a military response to this attack on the town of Prijedor on May 30th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: There was no military response at that time, not as concerns the civilian population, the non-Serb civilian population.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: With the exception of the army officer Zoran Karlica, who you identified who died several days as a result of the wound that he sustained on or about May 30th, 1992, were there other casualties?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: I heard there was another person, but I can't recall the name of that person.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know or did you learn whether any of the attackers, namely the Bosniak Muslims, were captured, wounded, or sustained fatal injuries?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: I can't answer the question because I didn't participate in the event, nor did I hear anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: At any time, sir, did you learn or hear that within this group there were purportedly Bosnian Croats who also attacked the town of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: I did hear that, and I understand there was a small number of Bosnian Croats among them.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Given the three incidences that occurred within this eight-day period, can you describe for us, if you recall, what the tensions were of the citizens within the Prijedor municipality immediately following May 30th, 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: The tensions culminated. However, there was no persecution. There was no ethnic cleansing. There were no murders, killings, or similar things.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Were the tensions high, average, or low during this period of time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: The tensions peaked at the time. They were high.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me take you, as I had before, through another period or section. And if permitted, I'm asking you to focus, Witness DD, specifically on the period following May 30th, 1992, up to and including July 21st, 1992. That approximate seven-week period is the period that the following questions will be addressed. Within that period, May 30th, 1992, through July 21st, 1992, did you observe or hear of any incidents, attacks, killings, or harassment by or against any ethnic group within the Prijedor municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: During that period, there was no harassment. There was no organised harassment, that is, by any of the ethnic groups against any other ethnic groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Were there any incidents similar to those that occurred in that eight-day period from May 22nd through May 30th, 1992, that would have occurred from the period of May 30th, 1992, through July 21st, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: There weren't any. Everybody stayed at home. Nobody was harassed. Nobody was taken away. Nobody was ill-treated.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Were tensions stabilised throughout that entire period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: They did, to a certain extent.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: To what extent?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: The life became more or less normal again.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you, sir, continue to work during that period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: I did. I went to work every day, and I performed the duties that I have already described.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And you travelled, sir, as you've described, from Ljubija to Prijedor on a regular and consistent and continuous basis, correct, during that period again, May 30th through July 21st, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. As need may have been, and that need mostly occurred every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Were you able to observe, sir, within that period of time, May 30th through July 21st, 1992, whether Bosniak Muslims and Croats likewise were gainfully employed and going to work during this period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Yes. They did work to the extent that was possible, because some of the companies were closed down, but some public institutions continued working, such as the healthcare, the judiciary, the police, and similar public services.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Were you able, sir, to observe whether Bosniak Muslims and Croatians were employed, for example, in the health centre in Ljubija during this time period, May 30th through July 21st, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: To the same extent as prior to the critical 30th of April. I personally witnessed that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just so that I may have a concrete answer, is that a yes, no, or you're not sure? I don't want to leave it open for interpretation.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: I won't leave it open. The answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, sir - and we're moving right along - to what significance do you attribute the date of July 21st, 1992, if any?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: I believe that there was an incident on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And on that day, there was an incident --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: On that day -- actually, it was in the evening of that day. In a village close to Hambarine, the village called Rizvanovici - and I can now see it on the ELMO --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just so the record is clear, when you're pointing, Witness DD, you're pointing to that which is on the right of the identified town of Rizvanovici, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: This is Rizvanovici, and yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Share with us, if you will, the circumstances surrounding the incident which occurred in the evening of July 21st, 1992, to the best of your recollection.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Two soldiers were killed by armed Muslims, and this is how the incident took place. The soldiers, whose last names were Joskic and Daljevic, were standing guard in the village of Rizvanovici, and during that night the villagers called them from a house - I don't know which house that was - they invited them in to have a cup of coffee, and the soldiers did that. And they stayed in the house with the hosts for about half an hour, up to an hour, and then fire was opened on them. I can't remember exactly whether that happened in the house or when they left the house, so outside the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] You gave us the name of Joskic and --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: You gave us the name of Joskic and Daljevic. Is it Zoran Joskic? Would that be his first name, so we can be precise?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: I believe the name was Zoran.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you recall the first name of the soldier who was killed on or about July 21st by the name of Daljevic, what his first name was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: I can't remember his name, but I knew both of the soldiers personally, because they resided some 5 kilometres away from my house in a village called Ljeskare in the direction of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Is that village depicted on the map that the Prosecutor entered into evidence as S1?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: That village is not depicted on the map. The name of that village is not on the map, but I can point to the place where that village is. The name of the village is Ljeskare and that is the village where the two soldiers resided, if that is what you meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just so the record is clear, the village, as we can see it, within this map, Exhibit S1, appears approximately near or where the letter "H" on the word Hambarine appears, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Clarify for me, if you will, what these two military soldiers were doing in Rizvanovici on or about July 21st, 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: They had to stand guard, to provide security for soldiers or any other citizen and to prevent further clashes or armed attacks by those who did not belong to the army and similar people.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, how long these two villages were standing guard in the town of Rizvanovici prior to July 21st, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: I can't tell you that. I can't remember. But I believe that it was a couple of days prior to that because there was a daily change-over of guards. There were daily shifts.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Was there, to the best of your recollection, any type of ultimatum issued by the military in connection with the death of its two soldiers on or about July 21st, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
