utterances.text: There was no ultimatum, but the army organised itself. They reached Hambarine on the following day.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I can just interrupt you for a moment. We'll get to that; however, let me just clarify a couple other issues. Was there an ultimatum by the police authorities against the citizens of the town of Rizvanovici on or about July 21st, 1992, as a result of these two soldiers being killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: There was no ultimatum because the persons who had been killed were army members. So it was under the authority of the army to issue such an ultimatum.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Was there, sir, an ultimatum issued by the civilian authorities from the Prijedor municipality regarding the two soldiers that were killed on July 21st, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Again, they did not have any such authority, because again, the two persons killed were members of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did the military, sir, I believe as you were starting to explain, respond to the killing of its two men after July 21st, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: On the following day, the military reacted in the following way: On the axis between Hambarine-Rizvanovici-Biscani, they wanted to gather all able-bodied men of Bosniak ethnicity in order to be able to control them because they believed that the crime had been perpetrated by an adult man who carried arms. It could not have been done by a child or an elderly person. The only people or the person who could have committed the crime was somebody who was able-bodied, who was fit for military service.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did the citizens of that area relinquish their arms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: I believe that this had been done even before, while it was still peaceful, up to 21st of July. So by the 21st of July, all the arms had been relinquished. The locals in the area who had licence to carry firearms had relinquished them. I'm talking about the firearms for which licences were issued by the Prijedor police. The authorities had a good enough insight into the arms which were legally possessed by the locals.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did the military, following their request, secure and arrest the able-bodied men of Bosniak ethnicity in the towns that you mentioned after July 21st, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Yes. It happened on the 22nd of July in the area between Hambarine and Biscani.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Were you, sir, at any time subsequent to this, specifically July 23rd, asked or requested by the army to assist them and act as an escort to transport any of these men to any detention centres? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Yes. It was on the 22nd of July. I was not on duty. I had a day off. So they came and asked me to join them.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The request came from whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Members of the military authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Was this request in your mind compulsory or voluntary? Could you have, in other words, rejected their request to assist in the escort of these Bosniak Muslims from that area, namely Rizvanovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: It's very difficult for me to say that; however, I did not turn down this request for the reasons of safety of my family. I wanted my family to be safe.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So you accepted their request. Did you, sir, in fact proceed to escort a bus of Bosniak Muslims from the Brdo region on or after July 22nd, the day following the killing of two soldiers, in 1992 July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Yes. I escorted one bus from Rizvanovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Describe for us, if you will, first the size of the bus, the number of people within the bus, and whether or not anyone else assisted you in escorting these people to a detention centre following the killing of these two military men on the 21st of July.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: I served as an escort to a normal-sized bus. It was a bus which served for local transportation within the town with more standing places than sitting places. The bus was full of people. Those who were not sitting on the seats were sitting on the floor of the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: There was a bus driver, I presume, on the bus along with you, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: There was a driver and there was another soldier with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: During your journey, which we'll get to in a moment, you were able to observe what, if anything, would occur to these Bosniak Muslims from the Brdo region throughout their journey, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Yes. I was an eyewitness, and I was not their escort, but I provided security for them and I made sure that nothing happened to these people during their journey.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: You were likewise on the bus, correct, with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Yes, I was standing by the driver, facing the passengers. My back was turned towards the windshield.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Describe for us where while you were on the bus this bus travelled. And if possible, can you utilise the map, S1, to show us the route that you took on or about July 22nd, 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: The route was from Rizvanovici on to Biscani; from there, on to Prijedor. It proceeded towards Kozarusa, Kozarac, and other places on the way, all the way to Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did the bus which you were in, did it stop at Prijedor or any other villages during this journey from the Brdo area to Omarska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: No, it didn't stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The first time that the bus would have stopped was when it came to Omarska, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Taking specifically just the time for this voyage, were any of the detainees on this bus at any time from the time that they were loaded on the bus to the time you came to Omarska mistreated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Nobody was mistreated. There was just me and another soldier as escorts and the bus didn't stop anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Were the people in the bus - again limiting you to the time frame of this journey - were they at any time beaten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Nobody was beaten. Those who had the place to sit were sitting on the seats. The others were sitting on the floor. And they faced the windshield, so their faces were turned towards the driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did anyone curse or harass them in any fashion during this journey or attempt to humiliate them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Absolutely not. The driver did his job, and the two of us did exactly what we were supposed to do very correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Were you armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Yes, we were, both of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How many people, to the best of your recollection, were in this bus that travelled from the Brdo area to Omarska on or about July 22nd, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: There were about 60 people.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, sir, was this the only bus that travelled with residents of the Brdo area from the Brdo area to Omarska on July 22nd, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: No, this was not the only bus. There were several buses. But this was the last but one.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you recall how many buses there were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly. I don't know. Buses were coming in turns, taking people there and coming back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt. How can you know that this was the last bus? Did you have control over all the buses driving, leaving?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was the last but one. The last came after my bus, the bus that I was escorting. And then there were -- there were no other buses after that. And there were no persons left to be taken anywhere. So the group in my bus was the second last group. I'm talking about people who were considered to be people of military age and possible perpetrators of the crimes that had taken place the night before.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Witness DD, to assist the Court also in its question, which we were hoping to get to, you were actually not allowed to exit and to drop off the people from the Brdo area at Omarska, correct? And you were sent to another detention centre, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Not that we were not allowed. We did reach Omarska. We stopped outside the iron ore mine factory in Omarska. A military unit was waiting for us there.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you depart the bus when you arrived at Omarska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Yes, I did personally, and the driver did too, as well as the soldier. All the other persons remained inside the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Were you engaged in a conversation with anyone from within the Omarska detention centre relating to the people who were on the bus from the Brdo region?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: A soldier, I think he was an officer, a military officer, approached our group and asked whether this was the bus bringing the people from the Brdo area, and I said, "Yes, this is a bus from Brdo, just like the next one coming after us." And after these next two, there would be no more coming from the Brdo area, because no people were left there to be taken anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did the Bosniak Muslims who were within this bus, did they depart the bus in the Omarska detention centre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: No, they didn't leave the bus for the simple reason that this officer, as I've referred to him, said that they couldn't take in any more people because they had no room left to put people up. He insisted that these last two buses go to Trnopolje instead. This same officer spoke to the military over at Trnopolje and they had given him the green light for the buses to leave for Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Was this, sir, your first visit to the Omarska detention centre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: The first and the last, within a period of about five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I recognise that it's a short period. Can you describe for us, sir, the facility itself to the best of your recollection, whether there were buildings or simply one building, whether there was a fence surrounding the area, et cetera. And also tell us, if you'd be kind enough, whether you observed any people who were within Omarska standing against the wall.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Firstly, it's an industrial zone we're speaking about. Of course there was a fence there, but this fence was no barbed wire fence or a fence through which you couldn't see outside. There are rooms there, buildings, and factory halls, or the buildings used for the operations of the iron ore mine. I saw a number of people outside one of the buildings just outside the factory. They were lined up against a wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] How many people approximately did you see lined up against the wall?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: My apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Approximately how many people did you see lined up against the wall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Perhaps about a busload of people, 50, 60 people. I don't know exactly. I can't remember. I didn't count them.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you observe, sir, at that time whether there were any corpses or dead bodies within the Omarska detention centre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Not that I saw any during the short time that I spent there. No people being beaten, no people being physically mistreated or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you see, sir, or were you able to observe any signs of any of the detainees of injuries that they may have sustained as a result of beatings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: As far as I know, as far as I saw while I was there, I didn't see any signs of possible beatings or other kinds of injuries or anyone that I saw there. The persons I saw standing next to that wall I talked about, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How about any other persons that you may have observed within that Omarska detention centre? Were you able to see or observe any injuries as a result of beatings on that day when you were there for that approximate five or so minutes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: From a distance of about 20 metres, I did not observe anything unusual.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Moving along, did you proceed then, sir, to escort or assist in security of this convoy of Bosnian Muslims from Omarska to Trnopolje immediately thereafter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Yes. Our orders were to take these two buses to Trnopolje. We moved down the following route: Omarska-Petrov Gaj-Trnopolje. That was the route we took.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: From whom did you receive these orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: From the military authorities in Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you obtain any such orders from civilian authorities or police authorities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: No. There was no way for us to receive orders from them, because there were no police or civilian authorities there at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you proceed to make it to the Trnopolje detention centre on or about July 22nd, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, the 22nd of July, sometime in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Had you ever been to the Trnopolje detention centre prior to this day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: No, never. Nor had I ever had the opportunity or a need to go there.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Describe for us, if you will, what you observed when you came to the Trnopolje detention centre on July 22nd, 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: As I've said, we arrived in the afternoon. I noticed some sort of a cultural hall with all the facilities and a spacious yard outside that building. There were quite a lot of people there, civilians, women, children, elderly people, military-aged men too.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Tell us whether or not there was a barbed wire fence that surrounded the Trnopolje detention centre on or about July 22nd, 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Where we arrived from, and as far as I can remember, there was no barbed wire. Even the fence around the cultural hall that I talked about was sort of half destroyed, pulled down, probably even before the war broke out.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Were you able to observe, sir, whether or not people were sleeping within make-shift tents outside in this spacious yard that you've identified before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: It was all inside the yard, and those who couldn't be put up inside one of the buildings or surrounding facilities were put up inside tents, because it was summer and it was quite warm.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Were there vehicles also within the Trnopolje detention centre that you observed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Aside from a number of civilian [as interpreted] vehicles, there were civilian vehicles there belonging to the people inside the camp, their tractors and the trailers.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honour, with all due respect to the interpreter, I think the witness said "aside from military vehicles, there were civilian vehicles that belonged to the citizens who were within there." But I'd ask just that we make a record of it and then we could obviously verify and correct that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, correction, military.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How long were you at the Trnopolje camp on this first visit there on July 22nd, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Well, first of all, I did not see it as a camp back then. I thought it was a collection centre where persons came -- at least, the ones who had arrived before the busloads of people I talked about -- in order to be given the necessary protection, because their houses had been destroyed. Most of the people there were people whose houses had been destroyed on the 24th of May or on the 22nd of May. I am talking about the Hambarine and Kozarac areas. Those persons' houses had been destroyed in combat operations, and they had nowhere to stay or no roof over their heads, so they just flocked to Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: To the best of your abilities and recollection, do you recall the number of people that were within this Trnopolje detention centre on July 22nd, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, about 300 or 400 people, but I can't say with certainty because I couldn't see everyone who was inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Were you able to observe, sir, whether there were men, women, and children within this detention centre on that date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Yes. As I've said before, there were women there, children too, elderly people, and military-aged persons. Whole families were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you, sir, observe while you were at the Trnopolje detention centre whether any of the people within that detention centre were beaten or otherwise injured in any manner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: I didn't see any such thing happening, and I saw personally, as concerns the people who were staying in the collection centre, the Trnopolje collection centre, I spoke to them. I asked them where they were from, how they arrived there, and how they were treated in the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just for the purposes of being thorough - I failed to ask you this question - during your journey from Omarska to Trnopolje on July 22nd, within that period of time, were any of the Bosniak Muslims who were on this bus in which you were providing security mistreated, beaten, harassed, or intimidated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: You mentioned that you were able to talk to some of the people within the Trnopolje detention centre. Did you discuss with them issues of living conditions and/or the supply of food?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: I spoke to them about everything. They told me that the living conditions there were not ideal. But most importantly, no one was touching them, no one was physically or mentally mistreating them. They had what could have been called sufficient amounts of food, they told me, and they had a place to sleep.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did they, sir, tell you that they were not being physically and mentally mistreated, or was that an observation that you made?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: I asked them, and during the hour that I spent there, I did not observe any of the individuals there having suffered -- any signs of physical mistreatment on any of the people I saw there.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you ultimately depart from the Trnopolje detention centre that day and proceed to go back home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: It was early in the evening that we left Trnopolje on our bus. The driver, my colleague, and myself, we went home. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Was this the first and only time that you went to the Trnopolje detention centre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: No, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: When, if you recall, following July 22nd, 1992, did you have an opportunity to go back to the Trnopolje detention centre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DD
utterances.text: Yes. I remember clearly. But for personal reasons, I would like to talk about this in private session, if that's possible, and with Your Honours' permission.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Would it be possible -- and I'll ask the Court for that -- do you know approximately the date, or would you like to have that also in private session, that you were next at the Trnopolje detention centre?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
